title: Pilot study of pesticide knowledge, attitudes, and practices among pregnant women in northern Thailand.
ehr_evidence: We administered surveys to 76 pregnant women in northern Thailand and used multivariable logistic regression to evaluate associations among pesticide-related knowledge, pregnancy trimester, and pesticide use behavior. Questionnaires were administered via face-to-face interview in Thai language by two study nurses.
summary: A pilot cross-sectional knowledge-attitude-practices (KAP) survey of 76 pregnant women in an agricultural community in Fang District, Chiang Mai Province, northern Thailand, assessing pesticide-related knowledge, attitudes, and risky behaviors using logistic regression.
key_findings: Lower continuous knowledge score was marginally associated with fewer risky behaviors at home (OR = 0.9, 95% CI 0.7–1.0, Wald chi-square p = 0.10) but not significantly associated with risky behaviors at work (OR = 1.1, 95% CI 0.9–1.4, p = 0.21).

In univariate analysis, first-trimester pregnancy was significantly associated with fewer risky behaviors at home (OR = 5.0, 95% CI 1.1–23.9, p = 0.04), but this association became only marginally significant after adjusting for education (OR = 4.1, 95% CI 0.8–20.6, p = 0.08).
Pregnancy trimester was not associated with risky behaviors at work (OR = 0.8, 95% CI 0.2–3.0, p = 0.68).
Among agricultural workers, risky behaviors at home were significantly associated with risky behaviors at work (OR = 2.2, 95% CI 1.1–4.5, p = 0.03).

In the final multivariable model of risky behaviors at home, farm work before pregnancy (OR = 9.5, 95% CI 2.2–41.8, p < 0.01), applying pesticides before pregnancy (OR = 12.2, 95% CI 2.0–75.1, p = 0.01), having a previous child (OR = 4.1, 95% CI 1.0–15.7, p = 0.04), and strong belief in child's susceptibility (OR = 5.8, 95% CI 1.4–24.7, p = 0.02) were significantly associated with engaging in risky behaviors at home.
population: 76 pregnant women (mean age 26.0 years) attending the antenatal care clinic at Fang Hospital, Fang District, Chiang Mai Province, northern Thailand; 45% agricultural workers
exposure_domain: Pesticide exposure (knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to pesticide use)
limitations: Small sample size (n = 76), limiting power to detect associations in subgroups such as agricultural workers.
Self-reported survey data with potential reporting/desirability bias, as participants may have wanted to please researchers.
Outcomes were proxy questionnaire responses (risky behaviors) rather than actual exposure measurements.
